The indicator light is wired in parallel with the heating circuit after the switch. When plugged in and switched on, the indicator light turns on but the water does not heat after several minutes. After disconnecting power and cooling, a multimeter test shows infinite resistance between the heating element terminals and continuity across the thermal fuse. The switch and power cord show proper continuity when tested. Assume a single fault exists and all tests are accurate.

Which component is faulty?

Options:
A. thermal fuse
B. on/off switch
C. power cord
D. heating element

Reply using only the option label.

A voltage test at the burner terminals shows 240 volts when the knob is set to high. A continuity test on the burner coil shows no continuity. An open circuit on the continuity test means the burner coil cannot conduct current and therefore cannot produce heat. Voltage present at the terminals means the control circuit is supplying power to the element.

Which component is faulty?

Options:
A. The wiring harness
B. The indicator light
C. The control knob
D. The burner element

Respond with only the letter of the correct option.
